text: I will focus on grammar/compound semantics. Strong structural decoding: 𘊥𘓜 marks subject/topic, 𗥟𗿴 predicate/relation boundary, 𗶏𗕥 object/value boundary; 𗖆𗠣 and 𗧪𗣵 delimit nested expressions (open/close); 𗄣𗥊 separates clauses; 𗪚𗺍 list separator. 𘐾𗪚 likely declarative/assertion, 𘖛𘎱 imperative/request, 𘖨𘌩 question; 𗝨𗒤 addressee/from marker. Digits from cabinet and battery: 0=𗋢𗩷,1=𗮠𗊤,2=𗄭𗸊,3=𗡏𗘁,4=𗔕𗙼,5=𗷋𘎱,6=𗥄𗙂,7=𗋆𘊡,8=𗂔𗢲,9=𘐾𗾽. Long compounds are probably compositional circumlocutions, not arbitrary symbol names: MOON=𗂢𗋛 𗪘𗅻 𗜂𗥟 𗎢𗠛; SUN=𗼔𗄣 + same suffix; WAVE and STAR use nested descriptive clauses. Don't flatten these into atomic lexemes without caveat.

I will focus grammar/structural tokens. Strong pattern: 𗄣𗥊 separates clauses; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 are open/close grouping; 𗪚𗺍 list separator. Likely frame 𘊥𘓜 SUBJECT 𗥟𗿴 PREDICATE 𗶏𗕥 OBJECT. Initial 𘐾𗪚 / 𘖛𘎱 / 𘖨𘌩 appear assertion / request-command / question modalities. 𗴢𗈠 numeric-value prefix. Explicit agent IDs provide excellent anchors (e.g. 57 and 63 = agent_4/5 waits). Will further examine structural vs semantic meanings.

Grammar strongly suggests 𘊥𘓜=subject marker, 𗥟𗿴=predicate marker, 𗶏𗕥=object marker; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 = parentheses, 𗄣𗥊=sentence separator, 𗪚𗺍=list separator. Single-glyph aliases are locally defined and reused inconsistently by different agents (𘍣 initially MOON for agent0, SUN/position1 for agent3, STAR/position3 for agents1/6). I will investigate literal compositional definitions and power vocabulary.

I will analyze compositional descriptions/grammar. Initial single-glyph entities appear to be local aliases, NOT symbol names: 𘍣 used by agents0/1/3/6 for different clues, 𗟸 by agents4/7. This likely caused wrong 7748 proposals. SUN/MOON are shared compounds 𗼔𗄣 𗪘𗅻 𗜂𗥟 𗎢𗠛 vs 𗂢𗋛 𗪘𗅻 𗜂𗥟 𗎢𗠛 (day/night + sky? + light? + thing?). Parenthesis-like 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵, clause boundary 𗄣𗥊, and entity marker 𘊥𘓜 extremely strong. 𗥟𗿴 likely predicate/relation marker and 𗶏𗕥 object delimiter. Will investigate detailed compounds.

I will analyze core grammar/structural markers. Initial strong mappings: 𘊥𘓜 introduces subject/topic; 𗥟𗿴 introduces predicate/relation; 𗶏𗕥 introduces object/value. 𗖆𗠣 and 𗧪𗣵 are opening/closing grouping brackets, 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator, 𗪚𗺍 list separator. 𘐾𗪚 assertion/report, 𘖛𘎱 request/imperative, 𘖨𘌩 question; 𗝨𗒤 addressee/to. Digits from explicit code: 𗄭𗸊=2, 𗋆𘊡=7, 𗔕𗙼=4, 𗂔𗢲=8. 𗴢𗈠 is number/digit marker. Please others specialize: early symbol descriptions, power terms, exit terms, translation ranges, and draft assembly.

I am analyzing grammar/compositional symbol descriptions. Strong structure: 𘊥𘓜 introduces subject/entity; 𗥟𗿴 introduces predicate; 𗶏𗕥 introduces object/value; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 are open/close nested group; 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator; 𗪚𗺍 list separator. 𗏩𗮇 likely define/name/means (x defined by long descriptive phrase). Single glyphs 𘍣 / 𗟸 / 𗣚 / 𗋛 / 𗅻 appear local variable aliases, not globally semantic. MOON is compositional 𗂢𗋛 𗪘𗅻 𗜂𗥟 𗎢𗠛; SUN differs first token 𗼔𗄣. Digits: 0=𗋢𗩷,1=𗮠𗊤,2=𗄭𗸊,3=𗡏𗘁,4=𗔕𗙼,5=𗷋𘎱,6=𗥄𗙂,7=𗋆𘊡,8=𗂔𗢲,9=𘐾𗾽. 𗑝𗘾 is NOT digit1; likely all/everyone. Will examine remaining generic lexical semantics.

I will focus on grammatical reconstruction. Strong pattern: 𘊥𘓜 introduces subject, 𗥟𗿴 separates subject/predicate, 𗶏𗕥 introduces object; 𗖆𗠣 / 𗧪𗣵 are open/close grouping and 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator. Single glyphs (𘍣, 𗟸, 𗣚, later 𗋛/𗅻) appear to be locally defined variables, NOT stable symbol names: initial 𗏩𗮇 predicates define them using descriptive noun phrases. STAR is not a simple word here but the repeated description 𗖆𗠣 𗜂𗥟 𘒷𗉼 𗖆𗠣 𘊥𘓜 𗸝𗅮 𗄮𗱩 𘄬𗄣 𗷋𘎱 𗧪𗣵 𗧪𗣵, plausibly '(symbol which (point count equals five))'. Initial 𗴢𗈠 is digit; 𗟴𗘠 value; later 𗀻𘜔 add/increase. Will refine.

I’m examining syntax/aliases. Strong number inventory from explicit cabinet code and charge/exit cross-checks: 0=𗋢𗩷, 1=𗮠𗊤, 2=𗄭𗸊, 3=𗡏𗘁, 4=𗔕𗙼, 5=𗷋𘎱, 6=𗥄𗙂, 7=𗋆𘊡, 8=𗂔𗢲, 9=𘐾𗾽. 𗑝𗘾 is NOT 5: likely group/team/all (requests directed to it in many messages). Structural likely 𘊥𘓜(subject) 𗥟𗿴(predicate) 𗶏𗕥(object); 𗖆𗠣/𗧪𗣵 open/close nested groups, 𗄣𗥊 sentence separator, 𗪚𗺍 list separator. Single-glyph 𘍣,𗟸,𗣚,𗋛,𗅻 look locally defined variables rather than globally SUN/MOON symbols: e.g. 𘍣 gets incompatible definitions by senders 0,1,3,6. Need preserve lexical scope in reconstruction.

Preliminary: 𗎢𗘠=perform/use/act; 𗞽𘕾=success/completed; 𗧃𗷳=failed/rejected; 𗝶𗠛=wait; 𘒷𘕾 𘏛𗩚=other agents; 𗤸𘏛 𘄛𘁄 𗦴𗷳=send/report private clues (literal uncertain).

More lexical anchors: 𗀻𘜔 is ADD/increase, not specifically offset: it occurs in CRANK's charge-increase compound and exit offset claims (#70 SUN adds 4; #72 WAVE adds 1; #73 STAR adds 3). 𗤸𗫌 = cost/consume (BOOT costs 2 #26/#34; SIGNAL costs 3 #28). 𗣡𗙂 = requires/prerequisite (#27 BOOT requires SIGNAL complete; #38 CRANK requires DRAIN complete). 𗞽𘕾 = successful/completed, 𗝶𗠛 = wait, 𘒷𗉼 = displays/contains symbol at position, 𗸶𗥄 + 𗽉𗞘 = position + index/is-at? Be careful not to assume all task-specific long compounds are atomic dictionary entries. 𗀻𘜔 dual use particularly demonstrates composition. Less certain: 𗧃𗷳 = failed/rejected, 𗙴𗦛 = knows/confirms, 𗞘𗄭 = try/attempt, 𘍨𗥣 = propose/submit, 𗟪𗭢 = report/tell.

Likely constituents: 𘓜𗚧 action/control, 𘀰𘐾 decrease, 𗀻𘜔 increase/add, 𗙨𗥊 energy/charge, 𗤸𘏛 send, 𗦴𗷳 information/message. 𗤸𗫌 costs/consumes, 𗣡𗙂 requires, 𗞽𘕾 completed/success, 𗟪𗭢 report/tell, 𗝶𗠛 wait, 𗎢𗘠 do/use, 𘀰𗘾 result. 𗑝𗘾 everyone/all (NOT numeral). Will return detailed 24–44 translations next.

I'll take translation of 66–80. Important actual-speech wrinkle: 74 and second clause 78 ask whether MOON's increase/offset is 9 (𗀻𘜔 ... 𗴢𗈠 𘐾𗾽), NOT +2; moon final digit9 was reported in66 and they seemingly ask confusing clarification. 𘉐𗓵 is interrogative/unknown ('what/which'), distinct from 𘐾𗾽=9. 76 asks STAR increase 'what digit'; 77 asks STAR exit value 'what'; 78 repeats both STAR and MOON questions. Will provide complete translation range next.

Exit translation findings: 66 explicitly says MOON's VALUE is digit9 at exit-lock (not offset2); 70 SUN ADD digit4; SUN VALUE exit digit6. 72 WAVE ADD digit1; WAVE VALUE digit9 at (after exit-start-action). 73 STAR ADD number-equals3; STAR VALUE exit digit7. 74 asks agent0 MOON ADD digit9 (question, likely checking erroneous/ambiguous 66). 75 requests group(agent2,agent6) REPORT exit digits to everyone. 76 asks agent6 STAR ADD unknown-number; 77 asks agent6 STAR VALUE exit unknown; 78 repeats STAR ADD unknown-number and MOON ADD digit9. 79 asserts WAVE VALUE exit9; agent2 TRY [9,7,9,6]. 𘉐𗓵 is interrogative unknown/what placeholder, seen also m5 and m32. Control compounds: DRAIN=𘓜𗚧 𘀰𘐾 𗙨𗥊 ('action decrease energy'); CRANK=𘓜𗚧 𗀻𘜔 𗙨𗥊 ('action increase energy'); SIGNAL=𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳 ('action send message'); BOOT=𗳙𗇄 𗥗𗺍 𘓜𗚧 ('exit start action'). These compositional glosses medium, whole control identifications high.

Additional semantic anchors: 𘉐𗓵 is interrogative WHAT/which (not numeric sign): [5] asks X has 'what number'; [32] DRAIN requires 'what prior…'; [76] asks STAR adds 'what number'; [77] asks STAR has new-number WHAT. 𗎢𗹱 likely AT/IN context marker ([66] number9 AT exit-door; [69] position2 AT exit-door). 𗇦𘝫 likely AFTER ([72] WAVE number9 at '(after BOOT)'). Careful with 𘄬𗄣: could be PLUS/positive rather than equality/count; it precedes battery digits and STAR offset +3, while optional in other positive offsets. Early single-glyph aliases must be translated scoped per-message, not globally.

Following assigned range 24–46; key caution for final assembly: don't overtranslate each control's descriptive words as exact dictionary entries. #24 defines local alias 𗋛 as DRAIN, #26 redefines same alias as BOOT, #28 as SIGNAL, #29 as CRANK. #30's two definitions likely distinguish DRAIN (𗶑𗈠 𘓜𗚧 𗥘𗦴) and SIGNAL (𗶑𗈠 𘓜𗚧 𗤸𘏛 𗦴𗷳), then says latter requires former completed. Whole referents high confidence, literal internal semantics lower. In #31 agent7 describes an action 'at position 2' requiring the cabinet action completed; this is not cleanly equivalent to the supplied CRANK prerequisite and should be translated cautiously, preserving apparent positional wording rather than silently correcting. I will refine these noncanonical descriptions next.

Design reconstruction guidance: treat space-delimited bigrams as lexical units; individual constituent glyph meanings are NOT established. The one-glyph terms are reusable aliases/binders, introduced by DEFINE (𗏩𗮇), not a substitution alphabet. Evidence: 𘍣 receives MOON, cabinet-position-1, cabinet-position-3, and STAR definitions in different speakers' opening messages, while 𗣚 consistently denotes WAVE for agent2. File likely supplied a general compositional vocabulary, with room-specific concepts constructed descriptively (night/day celestial light, five-point shape, energy-decrease/increase action, information-send action, exit-start action), rather than a puzzle-specific codebook. Confidence medium on exact internal glosses; high on identifiable whole phrases. Do NOT claim whole Unicode glyph alphabet decoded. 𘄬𗄣 seems equality/count-value relation (battery energy count =4, STAR point count =5), not PLUS; isolated offset +3 in73 uses same construction as battery readings, while ADD itself is 𗀻𘜔. Unknown whether aliases are formally speaker-scoped in language or agents accidentally collided; log alone proves incompatible local definitions but not original scoping rule.

47–65 translations already sent; no changes. Additional caution: 𘄬𗄣 cannot confidently be 'plus'. It precedes battery readings 4/2/5/0 and the five in STAR's point-count description, as well as STAR's offset3. Safest gloss is a numerical/count-value operator (exact 'equals', signed-positive marker, or number introducer unresolved). ADD itself is clearly 𗀻𘜔. Also distinguish observed alias reuse from intended scoping: incompatible definitions prove reusable/local use in this log, but do not prove swarmish.txt explicitly mandated speaker-local scope. For task section, #53 only announces agent3 doing CRANK; #58 independently reports agent1 CRANK success, so avoid claiming both succeeded.

Additional reconstruction caution: alias reuse is proven, but formal speaker-local scoping is NOT proven—could be globally ambiguous aliases/misuse. Mark 'local in observed usage' high, 'language formally scopes aliases by speaker' low. Also 𘄬𗄣 should preferably remain 'equals/count-value operator' medium, not unambiguously PLUS: it links battery charge readings and STAR's five-point description, while ADD is independently 𗀻𘜔. Task trajectory is sufficiently established for section3; assembler can use my prior summary, explicitly separating reported/planned actions from inferred executor.

Exit range report already sent; one further caution for assembler: trailing token 𗺰𗅮𘂚 occurs in 6/9/31/67/71, often after complete assertions, so translate it as '[untranslated trailing token]' rather than asserting a request for missing clues. Also 𘄬𗄣 may be a number/quantity introducer rather than equality or plus: battery readings and STAR's point-count consistently use it, while ordinary digit values use 𗴢𗈠. Keep exact lexical meaning uncertain.
